office_does: The county treasurer collects property and excise taxes, invests public money and pays debts for the county and about 80 local districts; it does not set tax rates.
race_blurb: Treasurer Jackie Brunson, a 34-year county employee, faces Republican Timothy Garrison, an accountant who qualified as a write-in and runs as a political outsider focused on rooting out fraud. Coverage is thin: neither has a campaign website or has filed campaign finance reports.

candidates.summary: Incumbent treasurer since 2019 and longtime county finance administrator, running on office modernization and experience.
highlights: Cites electronic excise filing, digitized records, cross-trained staff and lower banking costs since 2019 [S1]
Legislative chair of the state county treasurers' association, working on tools for delinquent property owners [S1]
Nearly 34 years in county government, including the Sheriff's Office and Auditor's Office [S1]
Endorsed by the Skagit County Democrats [S4]

experience.basis: Incumbent treasurer since 2019 with nearly 34 years of county finance and administrative service.

candidates.summary: Small business owner and accountant who qualified as a write-in and runs as 'a political outsider' focused on eliminating fraud.
highlights: Says he will focus on 'eliminating fraud and protecting every taxpayer dollar' by scrutinizing the office's transactions [S1]
Describes himself as 'a defender of the Constitution' who will not allow improper or unlawful transactions [S1]
Qualified for the general with 1,155 write-in votes, about 5% [S2]
Promoted on SkagitResidents.com as one of four 'constitutional' write-in candidates [S3][S4]

experience.basis: Runs explicitly as 'a political outsider' with private-sector experience against a 34-year county official.

spending.basis: Platform centers on reviewing and challenging how public money is handled to eliminate fraud (oversight pole); single pamphlet statement, no position on spending levels.
